get.description: To retrieve the list of available REST API endpoints in your Zoho CRM organization for a specific API version. You can filter the results by module, OAuth scope, or request method using the filters parameter.

200.description: Returns the list of available REST APIs with their paths, HTTP methods, OAuth scopes, and credit consumption details.

schema.description: Contains the list of available REST APIs and their operation types.

__apis.description: Contains the details of all the supported APIs in the API version given in the request URL.

items.description: Each object represents an API with its path and supported HTTP operations.

path.description: Represents the API endpoint for the API version in the request URL.

operation_types.description: Contains the supported HTTP operations for that API in that version.

items.description: Each object represents the details of a single HTTP operation supported by that API.

method.description:
Represents the supported request method for
that API. 

Possible values:

**GET** - Retrieve data.

**POST** - Create data.

**PUT** - Update data.

**PATCH** - Partially update data.

**DELETE** - Remove data.

oauth_scope.description: Represents the OAuth scope required to perform this operation.

max_credits.description: Represents the maximum credits that the API consumes.

min_credits.description: Represents the minimum credits that the API consumes.

ApiResponse.description: Shows a sample of the successful response with three APIs, including their operations.

get.description: Fetches the existing configuration for appointment preferences, including rules for deal creation, job sheet visibility, and mark as complete configurations.
get.x-zs-llm-description: Use this API to fetch the current org appointment preference configuration before sending updates.

200.description: Contains the details of the requested resource.

schema.description: Returns the appointment preferences configured for the Zoho CRM organization.

appointment_preferences.description: Represents the complete set of appointment preferences configured in the CRM organization.

show_job_sheet.description:
Represents whether filling out the job sheet is mandatory for marking an appointment as 'completed'.
Possible values:
**true** - Job sheet is mandatory for appointment completion.
**false** - Job sheet is not mandatory for appointment completion.

when_duration_exceeds.description:
Represents who has to mark the appointment as 'Completed' when the service duration gets over.
Possible values:
**mark_as_complete** - The appointment is automatically marked as 'completed'.
**ask_appointment_provider_to_complete** - User has to manually mark the appointment as 'completed'.

when_appointment_completed.description:
Represents whether a deal has to be created when an appointment is completed.
Possible values:
**create_deal** - Deal is created when any appointment is marked 'Completed'.
**do_not_create_deal** - Deal is not created when any appointment is marked 'Completed'.

allow_booking_outside_service_availabili.description:
Denotes if you can create appointments outside service availability.
Possible values:
**true** - You can create appointments outside service availability.
**false** - You can not create appointments outside service availability.

allow_booking_outside_businesshours.description:
Denotes if you can create appointments outside business hours.
Possible values:
**true** - You can create appointments outside business hours.
**false** - You can not create appointments outside business hours.

sharing_enabled.description: Indicates whether sharing of the associated record in appointments with the appointment owner is enabled.

sharing_details.description: Details about the sharing configuration for appointment-associated records. When sharing is enabled, the record associated in the appointment field is shared with the appointment owner with the configured permission level.

sharing_computation_status.description: Indicates whether the sharing computation is currently in progress or completed.

permission.description: The permission level granted to the appointment owner for the associated record.

deal_record_configuration.description: Contains the field mappings and layout details for record configuration in Deals from the Appointments module.

layout.description: Represents the Deals module layout used when creating deal records after an appointment is completed.

name.description: Represents the display name of the Deals module layout as shown in the Zoho CRM interface.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the Deals module layout.

field_mappings.description: Contains the field mappings that define how appointment and service data populates deal fields when Zoho CRM creates a deal automatically after the appointment completion.

items.description: Represents a single field mapping entry, containing the target Deals module field, mapping type, and mapped value.

type.description:
Indicates the type of field mapping applied to populate the deal field. 
Possible values:
**static** - A fixed value applies to the deal field regardless of appointment data.
**merge_field** - The field value maps from the appointment or service module data.

value.description: Represents the value assigned to the Deals module field during deal creation.

oneOf.description: Represents a merge-field expression that maps data from the Appointments or Services module to the deal field.
Represents a structured static value for lookup or complex deal fields, provided as an object with a name and an identifier.

field.description: Represents the Deals module field to which the appointment data is mapped.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the Deals module field.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the Deals module field.
Represents the unique identifier of the deal record configuration.

SuccessResponse.summary: Example of successful retrieval of appointment preferences with deal record configuration.
SuccessResponse.description: Shows a complete appointment preferences response including deal record configuration with layout and field mappings.

put.description: To update the appointment preference settings in your Zoho CRM organization, including booking constraints, job sheet requirements, deal creation configuration, and record-sharing settings.
put.x-zs-llm-description: Use this API to update org appointment preferences. Prefer fetching current values first for nested or dependent settings.

schema.description: Contains the appointment preference settings to update in the Zoho CRM organization.

appointment_preferences.description: Specify the appointment preferences to configure for the Zoho CRM organization.

show_job_sheet.description:
Represents whether filling out the job sheet is mandatory for marking an appointment as 'completed'. You can mandate job sheets only when **when_duration_exceeds: ask_appointment_provider_to_complete**.
Possible values:
**true** - Job sheet is mandatory for appointment completion.
**false** - Job sheet is not mandatory for appointment completion.

when_duration_exceeds.description:
Represents who has to mark the appointment as 'Completed' when the service duration gets over.
Possible values:
**mark_as_complete** - The appointment is automatically marked as 'completed'.
**ask_appointment_provider_to_complete** - User have to manually mark the appointment as 'completed'.

when_appointment_completed.description:
Represents whether a deal has to be created, when an appointment is completed.
Possible values:
**create_deal** - Deal is created when any appointment is marked 'Completed'.
**do_not_create_deal** - Deal is not created when any appointment is marked 'Completed'.

allow_booking_outside_service_availabili.description:
Denotes if you can create appointments outside service availability.
Possible values:
**true** - You can create appointments outside service availability.
**false** - You cannot create appointments outside service availability.

allow_booking_outside_businesshours.description:
Denotes if you can create appointments outside business hours. You can configure this preference only when **allow_booking_outside_service_availability:true**.
Possible values:
**true** - You can create appointments outside business hours.
**false** - You cannot create appointments outside business hours.

sharing_enabled.description: Set to true to enable sharing of the associated record in appointments with the appointment owner. When set to true, sharing_details must also be provided.

sharing_details.description: Sharing configuration for appointment-associated records. Defines the permission level granted to the appointment owner for the associated record. Required when sharing_enabled is set to true.

permission.description: The permission level granted to the appointment owner for the associated record.

deal_record_configuration.description: Specify the configuration for creating Deal records when an appointment is completed, including the layout and field mappings.

layout.description: Specify the Deals module layout to use when creating deal records from completed appointments.

id.description: Specify the unique identifier of the Deals module layout. You can get the ID using the [Get Layouts API](layouts.yaml#$.paths./settings/layouts.get).

name.description: Specify the name of the Deals module layout.

field_mappings.description: Specify the field mappings that define how appointment and service data populates the Deals module fields when a deal is created.

items.description: Each object specifies the details for each field mapping, including the target Deals module field, the mapping type, and the corresponding value.

type.description:
Specify the type of field mapping to use.
Possible values:
**static** - Set a fixed value for the deal field regardless of appointment data.
**merge_field** - Map the deal field value from appointment or service module data.

value.description:
Denotes the value of the Deals fields. The format of this key's value depends on the mapping **type**.

**Value for merge_field**: The datatype of this value is a string. To merge any field from a module, it should be specified like this **${module_api_name.field_api_name}**.
Example: ${Appointments__s.Appointment_Name}

**Value for static**: The datatype of this value is a JSON object. It contains the name and ID of the entity.

When you want to give static values that look up to a different module, make a GET API call of the specific module and provide the relevant ID and name of the record. You can also give standard text values enclosed in a string.
value.x-zs-llm-description: Use a merge-field expression for merge_field mappings and a static value or object for static mappings.

oneOf.description: Specify a merge-field expression that references appointment or service module data using the format **${!module_api_name.field_api_name}**.
Specify a structured static value for lookup and complex deal fields, provided as an object with a **name** and an **ID**.

field.description: Specify the Deals module field to which the appointment data is mapped. Use the [Get Fields API](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) call to fetch the API name and ID of the field.

api_name.description: Provide the API name of the Deals module field.

id.description: Provide the Unique ID of the Deals module field. Use the [Get Fields API](fields.yaml$#.paths./settings/fields.get) to get the valid API name and ID of the field.

get.description:
To retrieve appointment records from your Zoho CRM organization. 

Use the `page` and `per_page` parameters to paginate up to 2,000 records, or use the `page_token` received in a prior response to paginate beyond 2,000 records up to a maximum of 100,000. Each request returns a maximum of 200 records. 

Subform data is not included when retrieving multiple appointments. The API returns field values containing sensitive health data only when the Restrict Data access through API option is disabled in compliance settings.

200.description: Returns the list of appointment records that match the request criteria.

Success200.description: Illustrates a successful response for GET Appointments, returning two appointment records with their owner, service name, appointment times, and status.

400.description:
The request fails due to an invalid module API name in the request URL or an unsupported HTTP request method.
**Resolution:** The module API name in the request URL must be `Appointments__s`, and the request must use the GET method.

schema.description: Represents the error response body returned for a failed GET operation, capturing either an invalid module API name or an unsupported HTTP request method error.

InvalidModuleResponse1.summary: An error response for an invalid module API name.

value.message: the module name given seems to be invalid

InvalidModuleResponse1.description: Illustrates an error response when an invalid module API name is provided in the request URL, returning error code `INVALID_MODULE`.

InvalidRequestMethodResponse1.summary: An error response for an unsupported HTTP request method

value.message: The http request method type is not a valid one

InvalidRequestMethodResponse1.description: Illustrates an error response when the request uses an unsupported HTTP method instead of GET, returning error code `INVALID_REQUEST_METHOD`.

put.description: To update one or more appointment records in your Zoho CRM organization. You can update a maximum of 100 appointments per API call.

requestBody.description: The request body must contain a **data** array with one or more appointment objects to update. You can include a maximum of **100** objects per request. Each object must include the **ID** field to identify the appointment record to update.

SamplePutRequest.summary: PUT request body with two appointment objects for update
SamplePutRequest.description: Illustrates a PUT request body containing two appointment objects with a full field set, including appointment name, contact, service, start time, location, owner, reminders, status, and rescheduling fields.

200.description: Returns a confirmation for each successfully updated appointment record, including the record ID, creation and modification timestamps, and the identities of the users who created and last modified the record.

Success200.summary: Successful update of two appointment records
Success200.description: Shows a successful response for a batch update in which both appointment records were updated. Each result object carries a SUCCESS code, a confirmation message, and a details block containing the record ID, creation timestamp, modification timestamp, and the identities of the creating and modifying users.

207.description: Returns a mixed-status response when the batch contains both successfully updated appointment records and records that failed the update. Each item in the response array is either a success object or an error object with an INVALID_DATA code indicating an invalid appointment ID.

schema.description: Represents the Multi-Status response body returned when the update request produces a mix of successfully updated and failed appointment updates. The response contains at least one success and at least one error.

allOf.description: Constrains the data array to contain at least one success response object, ensuring the response always reflects at least one successfully updated appointment record.
Constrains the data array to contain at least one error response object, ensuring the response always reflects at least one failed appointment update attempt.

data.description: Represents the list of result objects returned for each appointment update attempt. Each item is either a success response for a successfully updated record or an error response for a failed update.

items.description: Represents a single result in the response array. it is either a success object containing the updated record details with a status code and message, or an error object indicating a failed update due to an invalid appointment ID.

Success207.summary: Multi-status response with one success and one invalid-ID error.

data.message: the id given seems to be invalid

Success207.description: Illustrates a Multi-Status response in which one appointment record updated successfully and a second record failed with an invalid appointment ID error, showing how partial success and error entries coexist in the same response payload.

400.description:
The request was not processed due to invalid or missing fields. 

**Resolution:** Verify that all required fields are present and that field values satisfy the validation requirements for the requested appointment update operation.

oneOf.description: Represents the wrapped error response body returned when one or more individual appointment update requests fail validation. Contains an array of per-record error objects.

data.description: Contains the list of error objects for appointment records that failed validation during the update request. Each object corresponds to one failed record.

items.description: Represents a single failed appointment update. Each object contains the error code, the affected field details, the error message, and the status.

schema.description:
Represents the error response body returned when the PUT request to update appointment records fails. 

The response is one of two variants: a wrapped array of per-record validation error objects, or a flat error object for request-level failures.

MandatoryNotFoundResponse1.summary: Error when required Appointment_For field is missing.
MandatoryNotFoundResponse1.description: Shows a MANDATORY_NOT_FOUND error returned when the required Appointment_For field is absent from the request payload at $.data[2].Appointment_For.

DependentFieldUnchangedResponse1.summary: Error when Rescheduled_From matches the existing appointment start time.

data.message: Reschedule_From and Appointment_Start_Time cannot be same

DependentFieldUnchangedResponse1.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_FIELD_UNCHANGED error returned when the Rescheduled_From value provided in the request matches the existing Appointment_Start_Time, as the new appointment time must differ from the current start time to constitute a valid reschedule.

DependentFieldUnchangedResponse2.summary: Error when reschedule information fields change without a prior reschedule.

data.message: Reschedule the appointment atleast once to Update the fields of Reschedule Information Section

DependentFieldUnchangedResponse2.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_FIELD_UNCHANGED error returned when reschedule information fields such as Reschedule_Reason are included in the request without the appointment having been rescheduled at least once, as those fields can only be updated after Rescheduled_From has been set on a prior update.

DependentFieldMissingResponse1.summary: Error when Reschedule_Reason is set but Rescheduled_From is empty.
DependentFieldMissingResponse1.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_FIELD_MISSING error returned when a Reschedule_Reason value is provided in the request but the required Rescheduled_From field is left empty, as Rescheduled_From must be populated whenever reschedule information fields are included.

DependentFieldMissingResponse2.summary: Error when cancellation fields are set but Status is not Cancelled.

data.message: To Update the fields of Cancellation Information Section, value of Status should be Cancelled

DependentFieldMissingResponse2.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_FIELD_MISSING error returned when cancellation information fields such as Cancellation_Reason are included in the request but the appointment Status is not set to Cancelled, as the Cancelled status is required to process any cancellation-related fields.

NotAllowedResponse1.summary: Error when Service_Name is unavailable at the appointment time.

data.message: Service is not available on the given time

NotAllowedResponse1.description: Shows a NOT_ALLOWED error returned when the selected Service_Name is not available at the given appointment time, as indicated at $.data[0].Service_Name.

NotAllowedResponse2.summary: Error when Appointment_Start_Time is outside business hours.

data.message: Appointment time does not falls under business hours

NotAllowedResponse2.description: Shows a NOT_ALLOWED error returned when the Appointment_Start_Time falls outside configured business hours, as indicated at $.data[0].Appointment_Start_Time.

DependentMismatchResponse1.summary: Error when appointment owner is not a member of the service

data.message: Appointment Owner is not a part of Service Members

DependentMismatchResponse1.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error returned when the specified appointment owner is not a member of the service associated with the appointment.

InvalidDataResponse1.summary: Invalid data error for Appointment_For module format.
InvalidDataResponse1.description: Shows an error when the Appointment_For field value has an invalid format, indicated by the api_name field in the details object.

InvalidDataResponse2.summary: Invalid data error for unknown module API name in Appointment_For.

data.message: the given module name is not exist in multimodulelookup

InvalidDataResponse2.description: Shows an error when the module API name provided in the Appointment_For field does not match a valid module in the CRM organization.

NotAllowedResponse3.summary: Error when appointment is completed without a job sheet.

data.message: Appointment cannot be marked as completed without creating the jobsheet

NotAllowedResponse3.description: Shows a NOT_ALLOWED error returned when an appointment is marked as completed but no job sheet has been submitted, as indicated at $.data[0].Job_Sheet_Created__s.

DependentMismatchResponse2.summary: Error when Status is set to Completed before appointment end time.

data.message: Appointment cannot be marked as completed before the appointment ends

DependentMismatchResponse2.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error returned when the appointment Status is set to Completed before the scheduled Appointment_End_Time has passed. An appointment can only be marked as Completed after the appointment time has ended.

DependentMismatchResponse3.summary: Error when a job sheet creation targets an incomplete appointment

data.message: Job Sheet can be created only for completed appointment

DependentMismatchResponse3.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error returned when Job_Sheet_Created__s is set on an appointment whose Status is not Completed. A job sheet can only be created for an appointment that has been marked as Completed.

DependentMismatchResponse4.summary: Error when Status is set to Overdue before appointment end time.

data.message: Appointment cannot be marked as overdue before the appointment ends

DependentMismatchResponse4.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error returned when the appointment Status is set to Overdue before the scheduled Appointment_End_Time has passed. An appointment can only be marked as Overdue after the appointment time has ended.

DependentMismatchResponse5.summary: Error when Appointment_Start_Time is set to a past date or time.

data.message: Appointment cannot be scheduled for past dates

DependentMismatchResponse5.description: Represents a DEPENDENT_MISMATCH error returned when the Appointment_Start_Time is set to a value in the past. The appointment start time must be greater than the current time.

MandatoryNotFoundResponse2.summary: Error when required unit key is missing from Remind_At.
MandatoryNotFoundResponse2.description: Shows a MANDATORY_NOT_FOUND error returned when the required unit key is absent from a Remind_At reminder object at $.data[0].Remind_At[0].unit.

InvalidDataResponse3.summary: Invalid data error when data array exceeds 100-record limit.

value.message: invalid data

InvalidDataResponse3.description: Shows an error when the data array in the request body exceeds the maximum allowed limit of 100 appointments per API call.

RecordLockedResponse1.summary: Error when appointment record is locked.

data.message: Sorry, you cannot perform this operation as the record is locked.

RecordLockedResponse1.description: Returned when the target appointment record is locked and the update operation cannot be performed. The response includes the affected field path and the locking action that prevented the request.

InvalidDataResponse4.summary: Invalid data error for Remind_At unit field.
InvalidDataResponse4.description: Shows an error when the unit field in the Remind_At array contains an invalid data type; the unit value must be an integer.

InvalidDataResponse5.summary: Invalid data error for an invalid appointment ID

data.message: the id given seems to be invalid

InvalidDataResponse5.description: Shows an error when the appointment ID provided in the request is invalid. Use the Get Appointments API to retrieve valid appointment IDs.

403.description:
The authenticated user does not have the required Zoho CRM profile permission to perform the requested appointment action. A NOT_ALLOWED error is also returned when the operation attempts to reschedule or change the status of an appointment that is already completed or cancelled.

**Resolution:** A CRM administrator must grant the appropriate appointment-action permissions in the Zoho CRM user's profile.

schema.description: Represents the error response returned when the authenticated user lacks permission to update appointments, containing a list of error objects that describe the permission failure.

data.description: Contains the list of error objects returned when the caller lacks permission to update the requested appointment records.

NoPermissionCompleteResponse1.summary: Permission denied to mark appointment as complete
NoPermissionCompleteResponse1.description: Returned when the authenticated user lacks the Crm_Implied_Mark_As_Complete_Appointments permission required to mark an appointment as complete. The request is denied with a NO_PERMISSION error.

NoPermissionRescheduleResponse1.description: Returned when the authenticated user lacks the Crm_Implied_Reschedule_Appointments permission required to reschedule an appointment. The request is denied with a NO_PERMISSION error.

NoPermissionCancelResponse1.description: Returned when the authenticated user lacks the Crm_Implied_Cancel_Appointments permission required to cancel an appointment. The request is denied with a NO_PERMISSION error.

post.description: To create one or more appointment records in your Zoho CRM organization.

requestBody.description: The request body must contain a data array. You can include a maximum of 100 objects per request.

SamplePostRequest.summary: Request body with four appointment objects covering varied statuses.
SamplePostRequest.description: Demonstrates a request body containing four appointment objects, each representing a distinct appointment status: scheduled, rescheduled, cancelled, and completed.

200.description: Returns a success response indicating that all appointment records in the request were successfully created.

Success200.summary: All four appointment records created successfully.
Success200.description: Demonstrates a success response in which four appointment records were created. Each entry in the data array contains a SUCCESS code along with the record identifier and associated audit timestamps.

201.description: Returns a success response indicating that the appointment record was successfully created.

Success200.description: Demonstrates a success response in which appointment records were created. Each entry in the data array contains a SUCCESS code along with the record identifier and associated audit timestamps.

207.description: Returns a multi-status response indicating that the create operation produced a mix of successful and failed results. Each entry in the response data array contains an individual status code reflecting whether the server processed that record successfully or encountered an error.

schema.description: Represents the multi-status response body returned when bulk creating appointment records. The data array contains individual result items, each independently indicating success or failure for the corresponding submitted record.

allOf.description: Indicates that the data array contains at least one success item representing a successfully created appointment record.

delete.summary: Delete one or more appointment records
delete.description: To delete one or more appointment records in your Zoho CRM organization. Note that this API will not delete any deals created on the completion of the deleted appointments.

200.description: Returns a confirmation that all specified appointment records were deleted successfully. Each item in the data array contains the record ID, a SUCCESS code, and a "record deleted" message.

Success200.summary: All three appointment records deleted successfully.
Success200.description: Shows a successful deletion response for three appointment records. Each entry in the data array returns a SUCCESS code, a "record deleted" message, and the corresponding record ID.

207.description: Returns a mixed-status response when the delete operation partially succeeds. Each item in the data array contains either a SUCCESS code with a "record deleted" message or an INVALID_DATA code with a "record not deleted" message, based on the outcome for each individual record.

schema.description: Represents the Multi-Status response body returned when a bulk deletion request results in a mix of successful and failed appointment deletion attempts.

allOf.description: Represents the constraint that the data array contains at least one successful deletion result, where each matching item holds the deleted record ID.
Represents the constraint that the data array contains at least one failed deletion result, where each matching item describes an appointment record that could not be deleted.

data.description: Represents the list of result objects for each appointment deletion attempt. Each item is either a success confirmation or an error response.

items.description: Represents a single result item for an appointment deletion attempt, which is either a success confirmation or an error response.

Success207.summary: Partial deletion where one record deleted, one failed with INVALID_DATA.
Success207.description: Shows a partial deletion response where the API deleted one appointment record and could not delete another. The data array returns a SUCCESS entry for the deleted record and an INVALID_DATA entry with a "record not deleted" message for the failed record.

400.description:
The request could not be processed due to an invalid appointment ID, an invalid module name, or an unsupported HTTP request method.

**Resolution:** For INVALID_DATA, make a GET Appointments API call and provide a valid appointment ID. For INVALID_REQUEST_METHOD, use only the DELETE method. For INVALID_MODULE, verify that the module API name in the request is correct.

oneOf.description: Represents the error response body containing a list of INVALID_DATA errors, where each item corresponds to an appointment record that could not be deleted.

data.description: Represents the list of error objects for the appointment records that could not be deleted.

schema.description: Represents the error response body for a failed DELETE Appointments request, containing either a list of record-level validation errors or a single request-level error.

InvalidDataResponse1.summary: INVALID_DATA error where appointment ID is invalid or already deleted
InvalidDataResponse1.description: Shows an error response when the specified appointment ID is invalid or the record has already been deleted. The response returns an INVALID_DATA code with a "record not deleted" message and the corresponding record ID in the details object.

InvalidRequestMethodResponse1.summary: Invalid HTTP request method type used in the request.

value.message: The http request method type is not a valid one

InvalidModuleResponse1.summary: Invalid module API name provided in the request.

InvalidModuleResponse1.description: Shows an error response when the module name in the request is invalid. The response returns an INVALID_MODULE code with the message "the module name given seems to be invalid" and a resource_path_index in the details object.

**Resolution:** Verify that the module API name in the request URL is correct. Use the [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to retrieve the valid module API name, and confirm that the appointment ID corresponds to an existing record.

schema.description: Represents the error response body when the module API name or the appointment ID in the request URL is invalid. Contains one of two error such as an INVALID_MODULE error when the module name is unrecognized, or an INVALID_URL_PATTERN error when the appointment ID cannot be resolved.

NotAllowedResponse1.summary: **NOT_ALLOWED** error when the service is unavailable at the given **Appointment_Start_Time**.

NotAllowedResponse3.summary: **NOT_ALLOWED** error when completing an appointment without a job sheet.

DependentMismatchResponse2.summary: **DEPENDENT_MISMATCH** error when **Status** set to Completed before appointment ends.

group_operator.description:
Specify the logical operator to combine the filter conditions in the **group** array.
Possible values:
**and** - All conditions must be satisfied.
**or** - At least one condition must be satisfied.

api_name.description: Specify the API name of the field to use in the filter condition.

field.description: Specify the field to apply the filter condition on. Refer to the [Get Fields](fields.json#$.paths./settings/fields.get) resource for valid values.

value.description: Specify the value to compare the field against in this filter condition.

type.description:
Specify the type of the filter condition.
Possible values:
**value** - Compares the field against a static value.

comparator.description:
Specify the comparison operator to apply between the field and value in this filter condition.
Possible values:
**equal** - Records where the field value exactly matches the specified value.
**not_equal** - Records where the field value does not match the specified value.
**contains** - Records where the field value contains the specified value.
**not_contains** - Records where the field value does not contain the specified value.
**starts_with** - Records where the field value starts with the specified value.
**ends_with** - Records where the field value ends with the specified value.

items.description: Specify a filter condition object that defines a single criterion for filtering records in the bulk read export.

group.description: Specify the list of filter conditions to apply to the bulk read export. Each condition must include a **field**, **value**, and **comparator**.

criteria.description: Specify the filter criteria to narrow down the records exported in the bulk read job.

query.description: Specify the query parameters for the bulk read job, including the target module, optional field selection, optional Custom View, and optional filter criteria.

file_type.description:
Specify the file format for the exported records.
Possible values:
**csv** - Exports records in CSV format.
**ics** - Exports records in ICS format, applicable only when exporting from the **Events** module.

post.description: To create a bulk read job in Zoho CRM. A bulk read job exports records from a specified CRM module to a CSV or ICS file. The job runs asynchronously; use the Get Bulk Read Job Details API to monitor the job status, and use the Download Bulk Read Result API to retrieve the exported file once the job is complete.

**ADDED** - The job has been created and is awaiting processing.
**QUEUED** - The job is queued and scheduled for processing.

**COMPLETED** - The job has finished processing and the result is available for download.

get.description: To download the exported records from a completed bulk read job in Zoho CRM. This API returns a ZIP archive containing the CSV or ICS file with the exported records. The bulk read job must have a COMPLETED state before you can download the result.

post.description: To create a bulk write job in your Zoho CRM organization that creates, updates, or upserts records in a target module from a previously uploaded file. The job is processed asynchronously; the response returns the job identifier that the get job details operation uses to poll job status, and an optional callback URL is notified on completion or failure.

schema.description: Defines the payload for creating a bulk write job, including the operation type, optional callback configuration, and the list of resource configurations.

character_encoding.description: Specify the character encoding of the uploaded file. Zoho CRM auto-detects the encoding when this value is omitted; supply a value to override auto-detection and force the file to be read with the specified charset.

operation.description:
Specify the type of bulk write operation to perform on the file.
Possible values:
insert - Creates the records from the file as new records in the target module.
update - Updates existing records in the target module without creating new ones.
upsert - Updates existing records and creates new records that do not exist already.

callback.description: Specify the callback configuration that Zoho CRM uses to notify your endpoint when the bulk write job completes or fails.

url.description: Specify the URL that receives the job completion notification. The URL must accept the HTTP POST method and be reachable from Zoho CRM servers.

method.description:
Specify the HTTP method that Zoho CRM uses to invoke the callback URL.
Possible values:
post - Sends the job completion notification as an HTTP POST request.

resource.description: Specify the list of resource configurations to process in the bulk write job. Each entry describes the target module, the uploaded file to read, and the field mappings to apply.

items.description: Specify the configuration for a single bulk write resource, including the target module, the uploaded file ID, the matching key, and the field mappings to apply when the job runs.

type.description:
Specify the type of the resource being imported.
Possible values:
data - Indicates that the resource contains record data to be written into the target module.

file_names.description: Specify the names of the files inside the uploaded archive that the bulk write job must process.

items.description: Represents the name of a single file inside the uploaded archive that the bulk write job processes.

module.description: Specify the target CRM module into which the records from the uploaded file are written.

api_name.description: Specify the API name of the target CRM module into which records are imported. Refer to the [Get Modules](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) resource for valid values.

file_id.description: Specify the identifier of the previously uploaded file that the bulk write job must read. Obtain this value from the response of the bulk upload file API.

ignore_empty.description:
Specify whether to skip empty cells in the uploaded file when updating records.
Possible values:
true - Ignores empty values in a column and updates only the fields that carry a non-empty value.
false - Updates the target field with the empty value supplied in the file.

find_by.description:
Specify the field that the bulk write job uses to locate existing records when performing an update or upsert operation.
Possible values:
id - Matches records by their unique record ID in the target module.

get.description: To retrieve the details of a previously created bulk write job in your Zoho CRM organization, including its current status, per-resource and per-file processing counts, the creator, and the download URL of the result archive once the job completes. The download URL remains accessible for up to seven days after the job completes.

200.description: Returns the full state and processing result of the bulk write job identified by the supplied **jobId**, including the per-resource and per-file counts and the download URL of the result archive.

schema.description: Represents the full state and processing result of a bulk write job, including the overall status, the per-resource processing summary, the job creator, and the download URL of the result archive.

status.description: Represents the current overall status of the bulk write job.  Sample values include **ADDED**, **INPROGRESS**, **COMPLETED**, and **SKIPPED**.

character_encoding.description: Represents the character encoding used to read the uploaded file. Returned with the value detected automatically by Zoho CRM, or with the value supplied in the original create request when it was specified.

resource.description: Represents the list of resource entries processed by the bulk write job, one entry per resource configuration submitted in the create request.

items.description: Represents the processing record for a single resource configuration in the bulk write job.

status.description:
Represents the processing status of this resource entry. 
Possible values:
**COMPLETED** - All records in the resource were processed successfully.
**ADDED** - The resource was queued for processing.
**INPROGRESS** - The resource is currently being processed.
**SKIPPED** - The resource was skipped without being processed.

type.description:
Represents the type of the processed resource. 
Possible values:
**data** - Indicates that the resource contained record data.

module.description: Represents the target CRM module into which the resource was written.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the target CRM module into which records were written.  Refer to the [Modules](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) resource for details.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the target CRM module. Refer to the [Modules](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) resource for details.

ignore_empty.description:
Indicates whether empty cells in the uploaded file were skipped when updating records.
Possible values:
**true** - Empty values in a column were ignored and only non-empty values were written.
**false** - Empty values in a column were written to the corresponding field.

field_mappings.description: Represents the field mappings applied between columns in the uploaded file and fields on the target module for this resource.

items.description: Represents the mapping between a single column in the uploaded file and a field on the target module.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the field on the target module that received the column value. Refer to the [Fields API](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) resource for details.

index.description: Represents the zero-based column index in the uploaded file whose value was written to the mapped field.

format.description: Represents the value format applied to the column when the field requires a specific date, datetime, numeric, or currency pattern. Returned as **null** when no explicit format was supplied.

find_by.description: Represents the field that the bulk write job used to match existing records for this mapping. Returned as **null** when no matching key was supplied.

default_value.description: Represents the default value used to populate the field when the corresponding column in the file was empty.

value.description: Represents the default value that replaces empty cells in the mapped column.

parent_column_index.description: Represents the column index of the parent record reference when the mapped field is part of a subform or related record. Returned as **null** when no parent column was supplied.

module.description: Represents the related module API name supplied for lookup-style mappings that resolve values against a sibling module. Returned as **null** when no related module was supplied.

file.description: Represents the per-file processing summary for this resource entry.

status.description:
Represents the processing status of the file within this resource entry. 
Possible values:
**COMPLETED** - The file was fully processed.
**ADDED** - The file was queued for processing.
**INPROGRESS** - The file is currently being processed.
**SKIPPED** - The file was skipped.

name.description: Represents the file name read from the uploaded archive.

added_count.description: Represents the number of records that were created from the file.

skipped_count.description: Represents the number of records that were skipped during processing.  The error column in the result file explains why each record was skipped.

updated_count.description: Represents the number of records that were updated from the file.

total_count.description: Represents the total number of records that were created, updated, or skipped during processing.

code.description: Represents the result code returned by Zoho CRM for the processing of this resource entry.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the bulk write job.

result.description: Represents the result metadata of the completed bulk write job, including the **download URL** of the result archive.

download_url.description: Represents the URL from which the result archive of the bulk write job can be downloaded. The download URL is accessible for up to **seven** days after job completion.

created_by.description: Represents the Zoho CRM user who created the bulk write job.

name.description: Represents the display name of the Zoho CRM user who created the bulk write job.  Refer to the [Users API](users.yaml#$.paths./users.get) endpoint for details.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the Zoho CRM user who created the bulk write job.  Refer to the [Users API](users.yaml#$.paths./users.get) endpoint for details.

operation.description: Represents the type of bulk write operation performed by the job, such as **insert**, **update**, or **upsert**.

created_time.description: Represents the ISO 8601 timestamp at which Zoho CRM created the bulk write job.

callback.description: Represents the callback configuration registered for the bulk write job, used to notify the configured URL when the job completes or fails.

url.description:
Represents the URL that receives the job completion notification.
Possible values:
http://requestbin.fullcontact.com/1fcimk51 - Sample callback URL recorded for the job.

method.description:
Represents the HTTP method used to invoke the callback URL.
Possible values:
post - The callback URL is invoked with an HTTP POST request.

post.description: Creates a new cadence (initially in draft status) with its follow-up tree and optional un-enrollment rules in a single call. custom_view cadences require a custom_view.id; manual_enrollment cadences must omit custom_view. Follow-ups reference each other via reference_id (a client-chosen string) so that parent/child links can be expressed in a single request before server ids are assigned. The cadence must be published and activated before it will enroll records.
post.x-zs-llm-description: Set reference_id to any client-chosen string on each follow-up to establish parent/child links before server ids are assigned; use the same string in parent_follow_up.reference_id on child follow-ups. After creation, the cadence is in draft - call POST .../publish, then POST .../activate to begin enrolling records.

post.description: Publishes a draft cadence by merging its follow-up tree, transitions, and triggers into the live cadence, and then clears the draft. Before publishing, ensure the cadence contains at least one follow-up and complies with the action count and active cadence limits. get.description: To retrieve per-follow-up execution statistics for the specified Cadence in your Zoho CRM organization. Each follow-up element returns an analytics payload whose structure depends on its action type: tasks (open, completed, and failed counts), schedule_call (created, scheduled, completed, missed, cancelled, overdue, and failed counts), email_notifications (sent, opened, clicked, replied, bounced, unsubscribed, and unsent counts), and whatsapp_message_notification (delivered and failed counts). Use the **filters** parameter to restrict results to a single action type, and the **follow_ups_executed_from** and **follow_ups_executed_till** parameters to restrict to a time range.
get.x-zs-llm-description: Pass filters as a JSON object with field.api_name set to follow_ups.action.type and value set to the desired action type. Use follow_ups_executed_from and follow_ups_executed_till (ISO 8601 datetime strings) to scope the time window. The response follow_ups array contains one element per follow-up with an analytics object keyed to its action type.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Specify the unique identifier of the Cadence for which you want to retrieve analytics.

parameters.description: Specifies the filter criteria to narrow the analytics results by follow-up action type and value.

schema.description: Represents the filter criteria schema for retrieving Cadence analytics, including the field, comparator, and value to filter by.

field.description: Specify the filter condition, including the api_name and value fields.

api_name.description:
Specify the field name to filter analytics by.
Possible values:
follow_ups.action.type - Filters analytics by the follow-up action type.

comparator.description:
Specify the comparison operator for the filter.
Possible values:
**between** - Filters records within a specified range.

value.description:
Specify the list of values to filter by.
Possible values:
tasks - Filters follow-ups with task actions.
email_notifications - Filters follow-ups with email notification actions.
schedule_call - Filters follow-ups with scheduled call actions.
whatsapp_message_notification - Filters follow-ups with WhatsApp message actions.

parameters.name: follow_ups_executed_from
parameters.description: Specifies the start date from which to retrieve follow-up execution analytics, in ISO 8601 format.

parameters.name: follow_ups_executed_till

post.description:
Enrolls CRM records into one or more cadences.
**Notes**
- Only Manual Enrollment cadences can be enrolled through this API.
- Available only in Enterprise edition and above.
- Supports Leads, Contacts, Deals, Vendors, and custom modules.
- A request may contain up to 5 cadence IDs.
- A request may contain up to 100 record IDs.

post.description: To cancel a meeting and send an email regarding the meeting cancellation to the participants. A meeting can only be cancelled if attendees have already been invited and the meeting has not passed its scheduled end time. To check the cancellation status of a meeting, refer to the $event_cancelled key in the response from the [Get Records API](record.yaml#$.paths./module.get).
post.x-zs-llm-description: Use this API to cancel an existing meeting (Event) in Zoho CRM and optionally send a cancellation notification email to all participants. Before calling this API, you need the Event ID of the meeting you want to cancel. You can obtain the Event ID by calling the GET /Events API to list events or from the response of a previously created event. The meeting must have participants, must not already be cancelled, and must not have passed its end time.

post.summary: Process multiple API requests in a single call
post.description: To bundle multiple Zoho CRM API requests into a single HTTP call, reducing network round-trips and enabling request chaining. You can reference the output of one sub-request in another using the format **@{sub_request_id:JSONPath}** to build dependent workflows. When **rollback_on_fail** is enabled, all successful sub-requests are rolled back if any subsequent sub-request fails.

schema.description: Specify the composite request configuration, including execution options and the array of sub-requests to process.

rollback_on_fail.description:
Specify whether to rollback the composite API request if any of the sub-requests fail. The default value is false.
Possible values:
**true** - Rollback all operations if any sub-request fails. Workflow automation actions execute only after all sub-requests succeed.
**false** - Process each sub-request independently without rollback.
This key cannot be **true** when **parallel_execution** is **true**.

parallel_execution.description:
Specify whether  to process all independent sub-requests (sub-requests with no dependencies/references) in parallel. The default value is true. If "rollback_on_fail" is true, then the default value of this key is false.
Possible values:
**true** - Execute independent sub-requests in parallel.
**false** - Execute sub-requests sequentially.
This key cannot be **true** when **rollback_on_fail** is **true**.

__composite_requests.description: Specify the API requests to execute as sub-requests within the composite call.

items.description: Each object represents an individual API sub-request, including the HTTP method, URI, and optional headers, parameters, and body.

method.description:
Specify the HTTP method for the corresponding sub-request.
Possible values:
**GET** - Retrieve data from the API.
**POST** - Create a new resource.
**PUT** - Update an existing resource.
**DELETE** - Remove a resource.
**PATCH** - Partially update a resource.

uri.description: Specify the URI path of the corresponding sub-request. The URI must follow the pattern **/crm/{version}/{endpoint}** with the regex `/crm(/.*)?/v[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?/.*`.

sub_request_id.description: Specify a unique identifier for the sub-request. Use this ID to reference the output of this sub-request. The accepted regex is `[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

headers.description: Specify the HTTP headers for the sub-request. The **authorization** and **x-crm-org** headers are restricted and cannot be used.

params.description: Specify the parameters for the sub-request.

body.description:
Specify the request body for the sub-request.

> **Note**
> - **Using References in Composite API Requests**: You can reference the output of one sub-request in another within the same API call.
> - **Reference Structure**: `@{sub_request_id:JSONPath}`
>   Where,
>   - `sub_request_id` is the ID of the sub-request whose response you want to reference.
>   - `JSONPath` is the path to the specific field in that response.
>   For example, if you create a Lead in one sub-request (sub_request_id : 1) and need to update it in another, you can use `@{1:$.data[0].details.id}` to dynamically fetch the Lead ID from sub-request 1 and use it in sub-request 2 to modify the same record. 
> - The `rollback_on_fail` and `parallel_execution` keys cannot both be set to `true`. If both are enabled, the API returns the `AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING` error.
> - All Delete APIs (except Notification APIs) support only record IDs in the URL. Bulk delete operations are not supported.
> - When `rollback_on_fail` is `false`:
>   - Workflows, approvals, and other automation actions are triggered as intended.
>   - The Composite API consumes one API credit.
> - When `rollback_on_fail` is `true`:
>    - **Workflows**
>      - Automation actions execute only after all sub-requests complete successfully and no rollback occurs. If one or more sub-requests fail and a rollback happens, the automation actions are not triggered.
>      - For example, consider the case where a workflow is triggered every time a lead is created with the company name starting with 'S'. In sub-request 1, a lead is created, whose Company name starts with 'S', and sub-request 2 edits the newly created record's company name so that it does not start with 'S'. Only after executing both the sub-requests the workflow will be executed. But in this case, the workflow will not be triggered because the newly created Lead's company name is already updated in sub-request 2, and the criterion for the workflow is not met. Consider another case, where in sub-request 1, a lead is created, whose Company name is 'Silicon Solutions', and sub-request 2 edits this newly created record's website. If none of the other sub-requests change the company name of this newly created record, after executing all the sub-requests successfully, the workflow will be triggered.
>    - When a rollback occurs, the Composite API consumes one API credit.
>    - When all sub-requests succeed, the Composite API consumes two API credits.
> - Each Composite API request consumes **five concurrency credits**, regardless of the number of sub-requests.
> - Each composite API reduces the sub-concurrency by one, while the sub-requests consume their respective sub-concurrencies.

### Allowed APIs
The following table gives the list of APIs allowed in a composite request. For these APIs, there are restrictions on the number of records that you can create, update, or delete in a composite request.

|  API | No. of records allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Get Org, Get Metadata, Convert a Lead, Get Layout Rules, Get Validation Rules, Get Custom Links, Get/Add/Update Roles, Get Profiles, Get Records' Count, Get/Update Blueprint, Get Variables/Variable Groups, Get Tags, Add/Remove Tags for a record, Get List of Attachments, Delete Photo, Get Currencies, Get Shared Record Details, Get Assignment Rules, Get/Add/Update Pipeline, Get Wizards, Get List of From Addresses, Delete Notifications | No Restriction | 
| Add/Update/Delete Users, Update/Delink Related Records, Add/Delete Variables, Create/Update/Delete Notes, Create/Update/Merge Tags, Add/Update Currency, Add/Update/PATCH Notifications, Create/Update/Upsert/Delete Records | 1 |
| Get Territories, Get Notes, Get Email/Inventory Templates, Get Notifications, Get/Search Records, Get Related Records, Get records through a COQL query, Get Deleted Records, Get Users | 25 |

NonSubordinateUser.summary: Non subordinate user assigned as record owner
NonSubordinateUser.description: Returned when a user tries to convert a Lead and assign the resulting records to a non-subordinate user. This error is triggered under two permission settings: 1) 'List subordinates only' (role hierarchy) - For example, if User2 (Manager role) has this permission enabled, they can only assign ownership to their subordinates (e.g., User3, User4) based on the role hierarchy, not to users above them (e.g., User1 with CEO role). 2) 'Territories and Sub-Territory Users Only' (territory hierarchy) - For example, given a territory structure: Root Territory → Territory A (User1, User2) → Territory B (User3, User4), and Root Territory → Territory C (User5, User6), if the current user (User1) belongs to Territory A, only users from Territory A (User1, User2) and its sub-territory Territory B (User3, User4) can be assigned as the new owner. Assigning a user from a non-subordinate territory such as Territory C (User5, User6) will trigger this error.

200.description: Successfully retrieved currency data.

items.description: Represents a currency object that includes metadata and formatting configuration such as symbol, decimal precision, and display rules.

prefix_symbol.description:
Represents the position of the currency symbol.
**Possible Values:**
**true** - Display the currency symbol before the currency value. This is the default value.
**false** - Display the currency symbol after the currency value.

format.description: Currency formatting rules including numeral style, decimals and separators.

numeral_system.description: Number formatting style: Indian (1,00,000) vs International (100,000).

decimal_places.description: Represents the number of decimal places allowed for the currency. It can be **0, 2, and 3.**

decimal_separator.description: The decimal separator separates the integer part of the currency from its fractional part. It can be a **Period or Comma,** depending on the currency.

thousand_separator.description: The thousand separator separates groups of thousands in a currency. It can be a **Period, Comma, or Space**, depending on the currency.

exchange_rate.description: Exchange rate relative to the base currency (supports up to 9 digits and 9 decimal places).

is_active.description:
Represents the status of the currency.
**Possible Values:**
**true** - The currency is active. This is the default value.

post.description: Creates a field update action that assigns a static value to a field, triggered by a workflow rule. For single-value fields, use a string for value. For multi-select and multi-user field types, use an array for value (for example, ['Call', 'Advertisement']). update_type (mandatory for multi-select and multi-user fields) specifies how to update the field and is supported only for multi-select fields: overwrite replaces existing values, append adds to existing values. dependent_fields specifies fields affected when the target field changes — primarily used for picklist dependencies, where one field's value controls another's valid options. For example, updating Country to India restricts the dependent State field to Indian states.
post.x-zs-llm-description: Adds a new field update action that sets a static value on a field when a workflow rule fires. Before calling: fetch field id and api_name from GET /settings/fields?module={api_name}. For Pipeline fields: get valid values from GET /settings/pipeline?module={api_name} and include Stage in dependent_fields. For Layout fields: get IDs from GET /settings/layouts and include dependent Pipeline. For Owner fields: get user id from GET /users and supply notify plus related_records. Body must have a field_updates array with one entry covering name, module, field, type ('static'), and value. The response contains the new action ID needed for workflow rule association.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the field update configuration to create. Only one field update can be created per request. For dependency-driven fields, include dependent_fields as required: Pipeline -> Stage, Layout -> Pipeline -> Stage (nested), Owner -> user object from Users API.

post.description: To upload one or more files to the Zoho File System (ZFS) in your Zoho CRM account. The API returns an encrypted file ID for each uploaded file, which you can use to attach the file to a file upload field, image upload field, or record image field through the Create or Update Records API. The file is uploaded using multipart/form-data with a required 'file' field containing the binary data of the file to be uploaded. The response includes the file ID, name, status, and other details. Can upload 10 files in a single request by repeating the 'file' field. Maximum file size is 20 MB.
post.x-zs-llm-description: The file ID returned is single-use. Once it is associated with a CRM record, email template, or any other entity via their respective APIs, the file ID is consumed and becomes unavailable. To reuse the same file content, upload the file again to obtain a new file ID.

get.description: To retrieve the binary content of a file stored in Zoho File System (ZFS) using its unique file ID. The file ID is provided as a required query parameter 'id'. If the file exists, the API returns the file's binary data along with appropriate headers indicating the MIME type and content disposition for download. If the file ID does not correspond to any file in ZFS, a 204 No Content response is returned. This endpoint is used to download files that have been previously uploaded to ZFS and associated with Zoho CRM records.

This occurs when the 'id' parameter contains an invalid file identifier, an empty string, or references a file that has been deleted or never existed. **Resolution:** Verify that the **id** parameter contains a valid encrypted file ID from a previous upload response.

get.description: To retrieve the status of a scheduled merge job in your Zoho CRM organization. Use the optional job_id query parameter to filter results to a specific job.

status.description:
Represents the current processing status of the merge job. 
Possible values:
**SCHEDULED** - The merge job is queued and waiting to be processed.
**running** - The merge job is currently being processed.
**completed** - The merge job has finished successfully.
**failed** - The merge job encountered an error and did not complete.

CompletedJob.summary: Example of a merge job completed successfully.
CompletedJob.description: Shows a completed merge job with its unique job ID and final status.

204.description: Indicates that no merge jobs were found for the specified master record.

400.description:
Returned when the request contains invalid parameters, module, or a business rule prevents the merge operation. 
**Resolution**: The request must be corrected based on the error code and the message returned in the response body.

post.description: To merge duplicate records in your Zoho CRM organization into a single master record. Supports field-level value selection from child records and file attachment management. If a child record has more than 1000 related records, the merge processes asynchronously and returns a job_id for status tracking.

post.description:
To retrieve the count of related records for a specified parent record in your Zoho CRM organization. Supports optional filtering by approval status, conversion status, category type, and field-level equality criteria. A single request can include up to 20 related list count specifications. You can use this API to get the count of records in the following types of related lists:

- **System-defined related lists**, such as:
  - Survey
  - Desk
  - Projects
  - Visits
  - Expense
  - Invoice
  - Subscription
- **Custom related lists** created via Lookup fields.
- **Custom related lists** created via Multi-select Lookup fields.
- **Custom related lists** created via Multi-module Lookup fields.
- **Related lists** created when history tracking is enabled for a picklist field.

get.description: Fetches the list of global picklists available in the organization along with their details. pick_list_values, used_in_modules, and associated_fields_count can be included in the response based on the "include" query parameter. The response can be filtered in three ways: use the "fields" query parameter to filter by key, so that only the requested keys along with "id" are returned; use the "filters" query parameter to filter the global picklists themselves by the value of a key; and use the "inner_details_filters" query parameter to filter the inner details of the global picklists. A 204 is returned when no global picklists exist.
get.x-zs-llm-description: Lists every global picklist in the org. Use the "include" query (pick_list_values, used_in_modules, associated_fields_count) to expand inner details; pick_list_values triggers the heavier getGlobalFieldsWithOptions fetch internally. Use "fields" to restrict the response to specific keys — only the requested keys along with "id" are returned, and a key repeated in the list is processed once. Use "filters" to select the global picklists by the value of a key — either a single criteria (field/comparator/value) or a group of criteria combined with group_operator — and "inner_details_filters" to filter the inner details of the global picklists. Only api_name, source and customizable can be filtered on in "filters" (customizable is boolean and takes only equal); anything else returns 400 NOT_SUPPORTED. Internal/private global sets are filtered out unless the caller is explicitly entitled. Returns 204 when the feature is unavailable and no internal sets are requested.

When the "fields" query parameter is given, only the requested keys along with "id" are returned. When the "filters" query parameter is given, only the global picklists matching the criteria are returned. A 204 is returned when no global picklists exist.

patch.description: To update a custom layout in your Zoho CRM organization, including renaming it, modifying profile permissions, enabling or disabling the business card display, and creating, updating, or deleting sections and fields within sections.

requestBody.description: The request body must contain a layouts array with one object. You can include a maximum of five sections per request, with no more than five fields in total across all sections.

RenameLayout.description: Demonstrates renaming a custom layout by supplying a new name value in the request body. The existing layout identified by the path parameter retains all other configuration; only the display name changes.

AddProfilePermission.summary: Granting a CRM profile access to a layout
AddProfilePermission.description: Shows a layout update request that grants a CRM profile access to the specified layout. The profile is associated with the layout so that users assigned to that profile can view and interact with it when working on records.

RemoveProfilePermission.summary: Revokes a CRM profile's access to a layout via the delete flag
RemoveProfilePermission.description: Demonstrates revoking a CRM profile's access to a layout by setting the delete flag on the profile entry. This removes the profile's visibility and usage rights for the layout without affecting other profiles assigned to it.

ToggleBusinessCard.summary: Toggle the business card display setting on a layout
ToggleBusinessCard.description: Illustrates toggling the business card display setting on a layout by setting the business card display property to the desired Boolean state. All other layout properties remain unchanged while only the business card visibility is modified.

CreateCustomSection.summary: Creating a new custom section within a layout
CreateCustomSection.description: Shows a layout update request that introduces a new custom section into the layout structure. The section is defined with a name and display configuration, providing a dedicated grouping area for fields within the layout.

AddFieldToSection.summary: Adding an existing field to a layout section
AddFieldToSection.description: Shows a layout update request that places an existing CRM field into a designated section. The field is referenced by its identifier and positioned within the section's field sequence without creating a new field definition.

UpdateFieldSequence.summary: Reorder a field's position within a layout section
UpdateFieldSequence.description: Shows how to reorder a field within its section by specifying the target field identifier alongside a new sequence or position value. The updated ordering is applied to the named section without altering any other field configuration.

DeleteSection.summary: Permanently removes a section and its field assignments from a layout
DeleteSection.description: Demonstrates permanently removing an entire section from a layout. Unlike moving fields to unused, this operation irreversibly eliminates the section and all of its field assignments from the layout.

MoveFieldToUnused.summary: Relocates a field to the unused items section without deleting it
MoveFieldToUnused.description: Demonstrates relocating a field to the unused items section of a layout without permanently deleting it. The field is preserved and can be reassigned to an active section at a later time.

CreateNewField.summary: Adds a new custom field definition to a layout section
CreateNewField.description: Demonstrates adding a new custom field definition to an existing section of a layout. The request specifies the field type, label, and target section, creating a field that did not previously exist in the layout.

MultipleFieldsAcrossSections.summary: Adds up to five fields spread across multiple layout sections in one request
MultipleFieldsAcrossSections.description: Demonstrates adding up to five fields distributed across two or more distinct layout sections within a single request. This approach reduces round-trips when populating several sections simultaneously, subject to the five-field-per-request limit.

CreateFieldWithAssociation.summary: Creating a new field with a Field-Of-Lookup association
CreateFieldWithAssociation.description: Shows a layout update request that creates a new field inline and establishes a Field-Of-Lookup (FOL) mapping to a related field in another module. This association allows the field to surface data from a linked record via an existing lookup field, connecting the two modules at the field level.

UpdateFieldWithAssociation.summary: Attach a Field-Of-Lookup association to an existing layout field
UpdateFieldWithAssociation.description: Demonstrates attaching a Field-Of-Lookup (FOL) association to an existing layout field by providing the field identifier together with association details that reference the lookup field and its related field. This pattern links two fields so that the layout can derive values from the specified lookup relationship.

AddMirrorComponentToSection.summary: Adding a mirror field component to a layout section
AddMirrorComponentToSection.description: Shows a layout update request that adds a mirror field component to a section. A mirror component reflects the value of a field from a related module, allowing users to view cross-module data directly within the layout.

delete.description: To delete a custom layout from a module in your Zoho CRM organization. When the layout being deleted has associated records, a target layout must be specified to receive the transferred records and profile associations. If the layout has an associated pipeline, the target pipeline and stage must also be provided. get.summary: Get field dependencies for a layout
get.description: To retrieve the list of field dependencies configured for a specific layout in your Zoho CRM organization.
get.x-zs-llm-description: Returns all picklist field dependencies for a layout. Use the Fields API to resolve parent and child field IDs and api_names. Each dependency maps a parent picklist field's values to allowed child picklist field values via the pick_list_values array. Dependencies where internal is true are system-defined and read-only.

200.description: Returns the list of field dependencies configured for the specified layout.

schema.description: Represents the successful response containing the list of field dependencies and pagination details for the specified layout.

map_dependency.description: Contains the list of field dependency objects for the specified layout.

items.description: Represents a field dependency object, including the parent and child field references, dependency metadata, and activity status.

oneOf.description: Indicates that the dependency applies to the main module fields and is not associated with any subform.
Represents the details of the subform module when the dependency applies to a subform field.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the subform module. Make a [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to get the details of the subform module.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the subform module.

sub_module.description: The API name and ID of the field that is mapped as the parent in the subform of the module. For non-subforms, this value is **null**. This key is present only when you fetch all the mapped dependencies in a module.

internal.description: Indicates whether the dependency was defined by the system or created by the user. Possible values: **true**, **false**.

active.description: Indicates whether the dependency is active in the layout. Possible values: **true**, **false**.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the field dependency.

source.description: Represents the source of the dependency. Possible values: **1**. It indicates Zoho CRM as the source.

category.description: Represents the category of the dependency. Possible values: **0**. **0** represents the default category.

info.description: Contains the pagination details for the response.

page.description: Represents the current page number in the paginated response.

per_page.description: Represents the maximum number of records included on each page.

count.description: Represents the number of records returned on the current page.

more_records.description: Indicates whether additional pages of records are available. Possible values: **true**, **false**.

SuccessResponse.description: Shows two field dependencies - one for a standard module field pair and one for a subform field pair - along with pagination details.
SuccessResponse.summary: Example of a successful response with field dependencies.

post.summary: Create a field dependency for a layout
post.description:
To create a field dependency between a parent picklist field and a child picklist field for a specific layout in your Zoho CRM organization.

**Prerequisites**

- The selected layout must contain at least two option-based fields.
- Supported field types are Picklist, Radio Button, and Multi-select Picklist.
- Multi-select Picklist fields can be used only as child fields.
- Parent and child fields must belong to the selected layout.
- When using subform fields, the parent and child fields must belong to the same subform.
To create a field dependency between a parent picklist field and a child picklist field for a specific layout in your Zoho CRM organization.
post.x-zs-llm-description: Creates a picklist field dependency. The parent and child must be picklist-type fields from the Fields API. A child field can only appear in one dependency per layout. The pick_list_values array maps each parent value's display_value to its allowed child values in the maps array.

pick_list_values.description:
Each JSON object in this array corresponds to a specific picklist value in the parent field, and consists of the following keys:
- **display_value** - string, optional - The display name of the picklist value of the parent field.
- **actual_value** - string, optional - The actual name of the picklist value of the parent field.
- **id** - string, mandatory - The unique ID of the picklist value of the parent field.
- **maps** - JSON array, mandatory - The **display_value**, **actual_value**, and id of the picklist value of the child field that should be mapped with the parent field.
