post.description: To bulk update the ownership of records in a specified module based on a Custom View, territory, or field-based criteria in your Zoho CRM organization. You cannot change the owner of related records using this API. You can change the owner of up to 50,000 records in a custom view. This API schedules the operation as a job and returns a job ID, which you can use to check the job status. Job statuses are available for up to 60 days. The Mass Change Owner API is available only in the Enterprise and Ultimate editions. The OAuth scope enforced is specific to the target module (for example, **ZohoCRM.change_owner.leads.CREATE** for Leads); modules without a dedicated scope fall back to a generic custom-module scope.

schema.description: Specify the details for the mass change owner operation, including the target Custom View, the new owner, an optional territory, and an optional criteria filter.

cvid.description: Specify the unique ID of the Custom View whose records are to be reassigned. Refer to the [Get Custom Views](custom_views.yaml#$.paths./settings/custom_views.get) resource for valid values.

owner.description: Specify the details of the user to assign as the new owner of the selected records.

id.description: Specify the unique ID of the user to assign as the new owner. Refer to the [Get Users](users.yaml#$.paths./users.get) resource for valid values.

territory.description: Specify the territory to use as the source of records for the ownership change.

id.description: Specify the unique ID of the territory. Refer to the [Get Territories](territories.yaml#$.paths./settings/territories.get) resource for valid values.

include_child.description:
Specify whether to include records from child
territories of the specified territory in the ownership
change.

Possible values:

**true** - Include records from child territories.

**false** - Restrict to records in the specified
territory only.

criteria.description: Specify the criteria to filter which records are included in the ownership change.

field.description: Specify the module field on which the criteria condition applies.

api_name.description: Specify the API name of the field. Refer to the [Get Fields](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) resource for valid values.

id.description: Specify the unique ID of the field. Refer to the [Get Fields](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) resource for valid values.

comparator.description:
Specify the comparison operator for the criteria.

Possible values:

**equal** - Matches records where the field equals the
specified value.

**not_equal** - Matches records where the field does not
equal the specified value.

**starts_with** - Matches records where the field starts
with the specified value.

**ends_with** - Matches records where the field ends
with the specified value.

**greater_than** - Matches records where the field is
greater than the specified value.

**less_than** - Matches records where the field is less
than the specified value.

**greater_equal** - Matches records where the field is
greater than or equal to the specified value.

**less_equal** - Matches records where the field is less
than or equal to the specified value.

**between** - Matches records where the field value
falls within a specified range.

**not_between** - Matches records where the field value
falls outside a specified range.

value.description: Specify the value to compare against the field using the criteria comparator.

post.summary: Submit mass convert job for leads
post.description: To submit a mass convert job that converts lead records into Contacts, Accounts, or Deals in your Zoho CRM organization. The job runs asynchronously and returns a job identifier for status tracking.

For example, if you give contacts in this array, the tags of the lead will be carried over to the contact that the lead is converted to. post.description: To update a specific field value across multiple records of a module in your Zoho CRM organization in a single API call. The operation supports two modes. In the non-scheduler mode, the caller supplies a list of record IDs in the `ids` array and the system updates those records synchronously, with a maximum of 500 records per request. In the scheduler mode, the caller supplies a Custom View ID in `cvid` and the request schedules an asynchronous background job that processes up to 50,000 records matching the view; the response returns a `job_id` that can be passed to the corresponding GET endpoint to track the job's progress. The Deals module accepts up to three fields per request; all other supported modules accept only one field per request. Email, lookup, multi-line, layout, and line item fields cannot be mass updated.

schema.description: Represents the mass update request payload. The payload must include the `data` array along with either `ids` for a synchronous update or `cvid` for an asynchronous scheduled update. `ids` and `cvid` are mutually exclusive.

data.description: Specify the array of objects, where each object maps a field's API name to the new value to be applied across the targeted records. The key must be provided along with either `ids` or `cvid`.

items.description:
Each object maps one or more field API names to the new
values to be applied. 


> **Note**:

> The Deals module allows up to three fields per object;
all other supported modules allow only one field per
object.
> Email, lookup, multi-line, layout, and line item fields
cannot be mass updated.

ids.description:
Specify the record IDs to be mass updated synchronously. Use
`ids` for non-scheduler updates that target a small batch of
records and require immediate processing. Use the [Get
Records API](record.yaml#$.paths./{module}.get) to get the
valid IDs of the required records.


> **Note**:

> - You can use either **ids** key or the **cvid** key, you
cannot use them both in a request.

> - Scheduler type(using record IDs):

>    - You can mass update a maximum of 50,000 records in a
single API call.

>    - Automation rules are triggered automatically when the
record count is less than 1000. When the record count is
greater than 1000, automation rules do not get triggered.

>    - If some of the records have invalid data, only those
records will not be processed in the API call.

> - Non-scheduler type(using CVID and territory ID):

>    - You can mass update a maximum of 500 records in a
single API call.

>    - Automation rules such as approvals, blueprints, and
workflows are triggered automatically.

>    - When you want to mass update records in a territory,
you must specify the custom view ID.

> - You cannot mass update Email, lookup fields, layout
fields, multi-line fields, and line items.

> - You can mass update up to three fields in the Deals
module and only one field in all other modules in a single
API call.

items.description: Each string specifies the unique ID of a record to be updated.

cvid.description:
Specify the Custom View ID whose matching records must be mass updated. Use `cvid` to schedule an asynchronous background job that processes the records in the Custom View. Use the [Get Custom View API](custom_views.yaml#$.paths./settings/custom_views.get) to get the ID of the requires custom view. 

The response returns a `job_id` that can be passed to [Get Mass Update Status API](mass_update.yaml#$.paths./{module}/actions/mass_update.get) to track the progress of the scheduled job.

> **Note**:
> The cvid key is supported for mass update via API in the following editions:
> - Enterprise
> - Ultimate
> - CRM Plus
> - Zoho One Enterprise

territory.description: Specify the territory whose records must be mass updated. This key is valid only when you provide a Custom View ID in `cvid`.

id.description: Specify the unique ID of the territory. Use the [Get Territories API](territories.yaml#$.paths./settings/territories.get) to get the ID of the required territory.

include_child.description:
Specify whether to include the records of the child
territories in the mass update.

Possible values:

**true** - Include the records of the child territories.

**false** - Restrict the mass update to the records in
the specified territory only.

territory.description: Ensures that the `territory` key is not provided along with the `ids` key.

oneOf.description: Represents the synchronous variant of the request payload, provided when records are targeted by a list of record IDs. This variant does not accept the `territory` key.
Represents the scheduled variant of the request payload, provided when records are targeted by a Custom View ID. This variant accepts the optional `territory` key.

BasicFieldUpdate.description: Illustrates a synchronous mass update that sets the `Venue` field to `Zylker` on the two records identified by their IDs in the `ids` array.
BasicFieldUpdate.summary: Example of updating a single field across multiple records.

NestedObjectUpdate.description: Illustrates a synchronous mass update that sets multiple fields on a single record, including a `Layout` field whose value is provided as an object with `id` and `display_label`.
NestedObjectUpdate.summary: An example of updating fields that reference nested objects.

CvidUpdate.description: Illustrates a scheduler-type request that mass updates the `Age` field on all records matching the provided Custom View ID.
CvidUpdate.summary: An example of scheduling an asynchronous mass update using a Custom View.

requestBody.description:
The request body contains the data required to perform the operation.


Mass update of records happens in two ways:


**Scheduler type**: When you specify a custom view ID and territory
ID, a job is scheduled in the background and the system returns a
"job_id". Use this job_id in the [Get Mass Update Status
API](mass_update.yaml#$.paths./{module}/actions/mass_update.get) to
get the status of the job. You can update a maximum of **50,000
records** in this type.


**Non-scheduler type**: When you specify the record IDs, system
updates the records instantly. You can update a maximum of **500
records** in a single API call in this type of mass update.

200.description: Returns the outcome of the mass update operation.

NonSubordinateUser.description:
Illustrates a per-record error returned when a user assigned
to a user lookup field is not eligible under the calling
user's hierarchy permissions.


This error can occur in the following cases:


- **Role hierarchy permission: List Subordinates Only**

The calling user can assign only users who are their
subordinates in the role hierarchy.

- **Territory hierarchy permission: Territories and
Sub-Territory Users Only**

The calling user can assign only users who belong to their
territory or its sub-territories.

For example, consider the following territory hierarchy:
    - Root Territory
        - Territory A (User1, User2)
             - Territory B (User3, User4)
        - Territory C (User5, User6)
A user in Territory A can assign users from Territory A and
Territory B, but cannot assign users from Territory C.

get.description: To retrieve the current status and record-processing counts of an asynchronous mass update job that was previously scheduled in your Zoho CRM organization. The job is identified by the `job_id` returned in the response of the scheduler-type mass update request. The response reports the job state along with the total, updated, not-updated, and failed record counts so that the caller can track progress until the job completes.

200.description: Returns the current state and record-processing counts of the requested mass update job.

Status.description:
Represents the current state of the mass update job.

Possible values:

COMPLETED - The mass update job has finished
processing all records.

SCHEDULED - The mass update job has been queued and
is waiting to start.

QUEUED - The mass update job is queued in the
system.

RUNNING - The mass update job is currently
processing records.

SUSPENDED - The mass update job has been paused.

FAILED - The mass update job has terminated due to a
failure.

post.description: Searches for records in the specified module that match the given search criteria. This API accepts the same search parameters as the GET /{module}/search API, but they are provided in the request body instead of query parameters. Use this API when the search criteria are too long to be passed as query parameters. You must specify at least one of the following search parameters: criteria, email, phone, or word. A maximum of 2,000 records can be retrieved per search, with up to 15 criteria conditions. Newly created or updated records may not appear immediately in the search results due to indexing delays.

get.x-zs-llm-description: Use this tool when you want to search records matching for the given criteria in param within single module in CRM

get.description: Retrieves the list of all modules available in the Zoho CRM account, including standard, custom, subform, and linking (MxN) modules. Supports optional filtering by `status`, `feature_name`, and `include` to control the scope and depth of the response. When both `status` and `feature_name` are provided, modules must satisfy both criteria. Returns all matching modules in a single response without pagination.

200.description: Returns all modules in the Zoho CRM account with their configuration details, permissions, fields, layouts, and related lists. All matching modules are included in a single response without pagination.

AllModulesWithVariations.summary: Complete module list with all variations
AllModulesWithVariations.description: Comprehensive response showing all module types including standard, custom, subform, and web-tab modules with their full metadata.

schema.description: Response body containing the array of module metadata objects.

modules.description: Array of module metadata objects returned for the Zoho CRM account, up to 600 entries, each containing configuration, capabilities, fields, layouts, profiles, and permissions.

items.description: Complete metadata for a single Zoho CRM module, including configuration, capabilities, fields, layouts, profiles, and related lists.

global_search_supported.description: Indicates whether global search functionality is supported for this module.

public_fields_configured.description: Indicates whether public fields have been configured for this module.

recycle_bin_on_delete.description: Indicates whether deleted records are moved to the recycle bin instead of being permanently deleted.

has_more_profiles.description: Indicates whether more profiles exist beyond those returned in the current response.

sub_menu_available.description: Whether a submenu is available for this module in the navigation.

lookupable.description: Indicates whether this module can be used as a lookup target in other modules.

profile_count.description: Represents the number of profiles associated with this module; 0 indicates no profile assignments.

module_type.description: Represents the type classification of the module; exposed only for pathfinder and orchestration modules. Possible values: `CONFIGURATION_ENTITIES`, `ENTITIES`.

cc_enabled.description: Whether CommandCenter functionality is enabled for email communications in this module; exposed only for orchestration modules and not applicable for API-supported modules.

deletable.description: Indicates whether records in this module can be deleted.

description.description: User-defined description of the module, up to 255 characters; null when no description has been set.

creatable.description: Indicates if new records can be created in this module.

inventory_template_supported.description: Indicates whether inventory templates are supported for this module.

modified_time.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the module, returned as a timezone-aware date-time string; null if the module has never been modified.

presence_sub_menu.description: Indicates whether this module has a presence submenu option.

triggers_supported.description: Whether workflow triggers are supported for this module.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier for the module.

api_name.description: Unique API identifier for the module used in third-party integrations; starts with a letter, contains only alphanumeric characters and underscores, and has no consecutive or trailing underscores.

plural_label.description: Plural display label for the module; returns the translated label when translation is enabled, otherwise matches `actual_plural_label`.

actual_plural_label.description: Original plural label of the module as stored in the database, without any translation applied.

actual_singular_label.description: Original singular label of the module as stored in the database, without any translation applied.

singular_label.description: Singular display label for the module; returns the translated label when translation is enabled, otherwise matches `actual_singular_label`.

isBlueprintSupported.description: Indicates whether Blueprint (process automation) is supported for this module.

visibility.description: Bitwise feature visibility flags for the module; the base value 1 indicates fully visible. Add flag values to hide specific features: 2=WEBUIHIDDEN, 4=TABMENU, 8=LOOKUP, 16=RELATEDLIST, 32=MULTISELECTLOOKUP, 64=MODULE_SETTING, 128=AUTOMATION, 256=TEMPLATES, 512=IMPORT, 1024=EXPORT, 4096=REPORT, 8192=API.

convertable.description: Whether records in this module can be converted to another module type.

editable.description: Whether records in this module can be edited by users.

emailTemplate_support.description: Indicates whether Email Templates functionality is supported for this module.

email_parser_supported.description: Indicates whether email parsing is supported for this module.

filter_supported.description: Indicates whether records in this module can be filtered.

show_as_tab.description: Indicates whether the module appears as a tab in the main navigation.

web_link.description: URL for web tab modules; supports dynamic parameter substitution via the arguments array.

viewable.description: Whether records in this module can be viewed.

api_supported.description: Whether API operations are supported for this module.

quick_create.description: Indicates whether the quick create form is available for this module.

generated_type.description: Method by which this module was generated or created.

static_subform_properties.description: Configuration properties for static subform modules, including the list of field references.

fields.description: Array of field references included in the static subform, up to 25 entries.

items.description: Represents the field reference object containing the field API name and unique identifier.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the static subform field.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the static subform field.

feeds_required.description: Indicates whether activity feeds are required for this module.

scoring_supported.description: Indicates whether lead or record scoring functionality is supported for this module.

webform_supported.description: Whether webform integration is supported for this module.

arguments.description: Array of argument objects used to substitute dynamic parameters in web tab URLs; for example, `https://...&id=${Users.User Id}&name=${Users.First Name}`. Duplicates are allowed, up to 50 entries.

items.description: Argument object that defines a URL parameter substitution, with a name (template key) and a value (field reference expression).

name.description: Key used in the web tab URL template to identify the substitution parameter.

value.description: Field substitution reference expression (for example, `users.recordId`) resolved at runtime for web tab URL parameter substitution.

module_name.description: Represents the display name of the module.

business_card_field_limit.description: Maximum number of fields that can be displayed on the business card view for this module; must be a non-negative integer.

access_type.description: Access control type for the module; `org_based` grants organization-wide access and `team_based` grants team-specific access. This value is immutable after module creation and cannot be updated via PUT operations.

private_profile.description: Private profile configuration for the module, containing the profile identifier and name.

name.description: Name of the private profile associated with the module.

id.description: Unique identifier of the private profile associated with the module.

track_current_data.description: Whether current data tracking is enabled for this module.

oneOf.description: User object representing the user who last modified the module.

name.description: Represents the name of the user who last modified the module.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the user who last modified the module.

oneOf.description: Null value indicating the module has never been modified.

profiles.description: List of profiles that have permission to view this module; may be empty for certain module types, with up to 203 entries.

items.description: Represents the profile object containing the profile identifier and display name.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the profile.

name.description: Represents the display name of the profile.

parent_module.description: Reference to the parent module if this is a child or related module; an empty object `{}` for standalone modules, `null` in some cases, or an object with `api_name` and `id` for child modules.

api_name.description: Represents the API name of the parent module.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the parent module.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the module. Possible values: `visible`, `user_hidden`, `system_hidden`, `scheduled_for_deletion`. This status is separate from the numeric bitwise `visibility` flags. It does not itself enable/disable individual features.

sequence_number.description: Represents the display order of the module in the navigation list.

territory.description: Territory assignment for the module, containing the territory identifier, name, and subordinates flag.

name.description: Name of the territory; for example, "All Territories" when the ID is 0.

id.description: Unique identifier of the territory; 0 indicates the special "All Territories" territory.

subordinates.description: Whether subordinate territories are included in this territory assignment.

204.description: No modules match the specified filter criteria.

400.description: Bad request returned when the `status` parameter contains unsupported values or when `feature_name` is provided as an empty string.

oneOf.description: Error response returned when the `status` parameter contains an unsupported value.

code.description: Error code indicating invalid data in the request. Always `INVALID_DATA`.

details.description: Details about the validation error, including the parameter name, the invalid value index, and the list of supported values.

index.description: Zero-based index of the invalid value in the comma-separated `status` parameter.

items.description: A valid status value accepted by the API.

supported_values.description: Unordered list of valid status values; each value appears exactly once, up to 10 entries.

param_name.description: Name of the parameter that contains the invalid value. Always `status` for this error variant.

message.description: A message describing the validation failure for the invalid status parameter.

status.description: Status of the request. Always `error` for failed requests.

oneOf.description: Error response returned when the `feature_name` parameter is provided as an empty string.

code.description: Error code indicating invalid data in the request. Always `INVALID_DATA`.

details.description: Empty details object returned when the `feature_name` parameter is provided as an empty string.

message.description: A message describing the validation failure for the empty feature_name parameter.

status.description: Status of the request. Always `error` for failed requests.

schema.description: Contains the error response when the request contains invalid parameter values.

value.message: The status given is invalid.

InvalidStatus.description: Shows the error response returned when the **status** parameter contains an unsupported value.

value.message: the given feature name is invalid

InvalidFeatureName.description: Shows the error response returned when the **feature_name** parameter is provided as an empty string.

post.description: To create a custom module in your Zoho CRM organization. Only one module can be created per request. The required permission depends on the access type: **Crm_Implied_Customize_Zoho_CRM** for org-based modules and **Crm_Implied_Create_Team_Module** for team-based modules. Submitting the same api_name multiple times will result in validation errors. The optional access_type controls module access model (org_based/team_based).

requestBody.description: The request body must contain a modules array with one object. Only single module creation is supported per request. access_type is optional and defaults to org_based. For team_based modules, do not pass profiles.

schema.description: Represents the request body structure for creating a custom module, containing the module definition in the **modules** array.

modules.description: Specify the module definitions to create. Only one module definition object can be included per request.

items.description: Specify the details of the Module definition object containing module metadata, optional access_type, profiles (not applicable for team_based), and optional display field configuration

singular_label.description: Specify the unique singular name of the module. Only letters, numbers, and spaces are supported.

plural_label.description: Specify the unique plural name of the module. Only letters, numbers, and spaces are supported.

api_name.description: Specify the unique API name for the module. The name must begin with an English alphabet character, must not end with an underscore, and must not contain two consecutive underscores. If omitted, the system generates the API name from the **plural_label** value.

access_type.description:
Specify the access type for the module.Defaults to org_based when omitted. Use team_based to create a team module.
Possible values:
**org_based** - The module is accessible based on organizational profile settings.
**team_based** - The module is restricted to team-based access.

profiles.description: Specify the array of profile IDs that determine which user profiles can access this module. Required for org_based modules. Do not pass this key for team_based modules. Duplicate profile IDs are not allowed.

items.description: Specify the details of a profile to be granted access to the module.

id.description: Specify the unique ID of the profile to be granted access to the module.

display_field.description: Specify the details of the display field for the module. This is optional, but if provided, either field_label or data_type is mandatory. Supported data types are **autonumber** and **text**. If this is not specified, the system generates a text display field.  If data_type is 'autonumber', then auto_number configuration with start_number is mandatory.

field_label.description: Specify the unique display label of the field used as the module's display field. Either this property or **data_type** must be provided when specifying the display field.

data_type.description:
Specify the data type of the display field.
Possible values:
**autonumber** - Automatically generates a unique number sequence for each record.
**text** - Allows users to enter text values manually.

auto_number.description: Specify the auto-number configuration for the display field. Required when **data_type** is **autonumber**.

prefix.description: Specify the prefix to prepend to each auto-generated number value in the display field.

start_number.description: Specify the starting number for the auto-number sequence. Only numeric characters are allowed.

suffix.description: Specify the suffix to append to each auto-generated number value in the display field.

if.description: Checks whether the module's access_type is team_based to determine profile requirements.

then.description: When access_type is team_based, profiles must not be provided

not.description: Profiles must not be provided when access_type is team_based

profiles.description: List of profiles associated with the module

items.description: Profile object

else.description: Profiles configuration for non-team-based access types

profiles.description: List of profiles associated with the module

items.description: Profile object

Represents the status code of the module creation operation.

Represents the confirmation message for the module creation operation.

status.description:
Represents the overall status of the module creation operation.

**success** - The module creation completed successfully.

400.description:
The request failed validation.
**Resolution:** Verify that all required fields are provided with valid values. Returned when input data fails validation (invalid module properties, duplicate api_name, missing required fields, field length exceeded, unsupported operations, or mandatory fields not found). All modules in the batch must be valid; no partial success occurs.

put.description: Updates existing modules in the CRM. Allows modification of module labels (`singular_label`, `plural_label`) and profile assignments. Supports batch updates of up to 100 modules per request. Returns 200 when all modules update successfully, or 207 Multi-Status when some succeed and others fail. Module `access_type` cannot be updated and must not be included in the request body. This operation is idempotent - submitting the same request multiple times produces the same result.

requestBody.description:
Request body for updating modules. Supports batch updates -
multiple modules can be updated in a single request. Partial updates
are supported: only `id` is required; `singular_label`,
`plural_label`, and `profiles` are optional and can be updated
independently. Profile updates use delta semantics: profiles without
`_delete: null` are added (if not already present), profiles with
`_delete: null` are removed. Batch updates may result in partial
success (207 Multi-Status response) if some modules succeed and others
fail. access_type is not accepted in PUT request payload and cannot be
changed."

schema.description: Batch update request containing an array of module objects to update. Each module requires `id`; other fields are optional.

singular_label.description: Singular display label for the module shown in the UI while referring to a single record (for example, `Contact` or `Deal`). Must contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, with no consecutive underscores, and cannot be empty.

plural_label.description: Plural display label for the module shown in the UI while referring to multiple records (for example, `Contacts` or `Deals`). Must contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores, with no consecutive underscores, and cannot be empty.

id.description: Unique identifier of the module to update. Must be a valid existing module ID.

profiles.description: Optional list of user profiles to add or remove from this module using delta semantics. Profiles without `_delete` are added; profiles with `_delete: null` are removed. Omit this to leave profile assignments unchanged.Each profile ID represents a permission set determining which users can view, create, edit, or delete records in this module.

notify_on_related_action.description:
Indicates whether the notification channel is triggered by actions on records related to the subscribed module.
Possible values:
true - Notifications are sent for related record actions.
false - Notifications are sent only for direct record actions.

channel_expiry.description: Represents the expiry date and time of the notification channel.

Indicates whether the notification payload includes the changed field values from the affected record.
Possible values:
true - The notification payload includes the updated field values.
false - The notification payload does not include field values.

id.description: Represents the unique identifier of the CRM field being monitored in the condition.

group_operator.description:
Represents the logical operator applied to the conditions within this sub-group.
Possible values:
and - All conditions in the sub-group must be satisfied.
or - Any condition in the sub-group must be satisfied.
null - No grouping operator is applied.

group.description: Represents an optional nested sub-group of field conditions within the parent group.

module.description: Represents the CRM module context associated with the field-selection condition.

token.description: Represents the verification token used to authenticate notifications sent to the callback URL.

info.description: Represents the pagination metadata for the notification channel list, including the current page, record count per page, and whether additional pages are available.

per_page.description: Represents the number of notification channel records returned per page.

count.description: Represents the number of notification channel records included in the current response.

page.description:
Represents the current page number in the paginated response.

**Note**
Use the page and per_page parameter to fetch records according to their position in the CRM. Let's assume that the user has to fetch 400 records. The maximum number of records that one can get for an API call is 200. So, for records above the 200th position, they cannot be fetched. By using the page (1, 2, 3 and 4) and per_page (100) parameter, the user can fetch all 400 records using 4 API calls.

more_records.description:
Indicates whether more notification channel records are available beyond the current page.
Possible values:
true - Additional notification channels are available.
false - No additional notification channels are available.

get.x-zs-llm-description: This endpoint retrieves the available pick list values for a specified field in a module. It provides detailed information about each pick list value, including its display value (with translations if enabled), reference value, layout associations, and metadata such as sequence number, color code, and usage status. If the specified field exists but is not of a pick list type, the endpoint will return a 204 No Content response. Note that this endpoint does not support pagination, so all pick list values will be returned in a single response.

post.x-zs-llm-description: Irreversible: the source pipeline (pipeline.from) is deleted once the transfer job is scheduled — the response returns only a job_id, not immediate completion. get.description: Retrieves records from the specified module in your Zoho CRM organization. Use the [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to retrieve the module ID and API name. Use "sort_by" and "sort_order" to control the sorting of records. To fetch up to 2000 records, use "page" (1-10) and "per_page" (maximum 200). To fetch more than 2000 records, use the "page_token" returned in the response. Consecutive page tokens can be used to navigate through up to 100,000 records. The "$has_more" key is returned when fetching a specific record and indicates whether more records are available in subforms, multi-select lookup fields, and multi-user lookup fields. To retrieve details of a related list, use the [Get Related Records API](related_records.yaml#$.paths./{parentRecordModule}/{parentRecord}/{relatedList}.get).

You must provide the layout ID field if you want to, include the layout specific mandatory fields in the API-level mandatory check. Include only the fields that are defined in your layout for API-level processing and ignore the rest.

put.description:
Updates one or more existing records in the specified module in your Zoho CRM organization. Use the [Get Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) to retrieve the module API name and the [Get Fields Metadata API](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) to retrieve the field API names.
A maximum of 100 records can be updated per API call. Use only Field API names in the input. You can update all fields supported by the Insert Records API operation.
When updating multiple records, the response array maintains the same order as the input records, allowing each response to be mapped to its corresponding input record. 
To update multiple subform records, specify the subform API name as a key within the record and provide the subform records as a JSON array. Use the subform field API names as keys within each subform record. For detailed information on subforms, refer to the [Manipulating Subform using Zoho CRM APIs](https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/community/topic/kaizen-124-accessing-subform-using-zoho-crm-apis).
Use the [Modules API](modules.yaml#$.paths./settings/modules.get) and [Fields Metadata API](fields.yaml#$.paths./settings/fields.get) to retrieve the API names of the subform and its fields. To update an existing subform record, include its record ID in the subform JSON array. Use the [Get Records API](record.yaml#$.paths./module.get) with the subform API name to retrieve subform record IDs.
When adding a new subform record, it is appended to the existing records. Passing an empty JSON array for a subform deletes all its records. To delete a specific subform record, specify its record ID and set "_delete" to "null". Deleting the parent record also deletes all its subform records.

post.description:
The Upsert API inserts a new record or updates an existing record based on duplicate check field values. If a matching record is found, it is updated; otherwise, a new record is inserted.
When using the Upsert API, the system checks for duplicate records based on the duplicate check fields. There are two types of duplicate check fields: system-defined duplicate check fields and user-defined unique fields.
System-defined duplicate check fields are predefined unique fields for each module. The system automatically checks these fields to prevent duplicate records. Refer to the System-defined Duplicate Check Fields section for module-specific details.
User-defined unique fields are fields for which the "Do not allow duplicate values" option is enabled. These fields allow users to define custom fields for duplicate checking. For more information, refer to [Mark a Field as Unique](https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/crm/customize-crm-account/customizing-fields/articles/use-custom-fields#Mark_a_Field_as_Unique). When a record is upserted, the system first checks for duplicates in these fields. If a matching record exists, it gets updated; otherwise, a new record is inserted.
You can specify the order in which the system checks for duplicate records using the "duplicate_check_fields" array in the API request. The array can contain system-defined duplicate check fields, such as "Email" for the Leads module, and user-defined unique fields, such as "Phone" and "Fax".
For example, in the Leads module, you can specify: "duplicate_check_fields": ["Email", "Phone", "Fax"].
If "duplicate_check_fields" is not specified, the system checks duplicate records in the following order: 1. System-defined duplicate check fields. 2. User-defined unique fields.

Provide the layout ID to include layout-specific mandatory fields in the API-level mandatory field check; only the fields defined in that layout are considered for processing, and the rest are ignored.

get.description:
To retrieve the total number of records in a specified Zoho CRM module, optionally filtered by a Custom View or search criteria. The count can be filtered using `cvid` (Custom View ID) or search parameters (`criteria`, `email`, `phone`, or `word`). These two filter groups are mutually exclusive - they cannot be combined in the same request. The `converted` and `approved` parameters apply only to the Leads module. The `type` parameter applies only to the Users module. Note: The record count may take 1-10 minutes to reflect the latest changes in Zoho CRM.

The count can be filtered using `cvid` (Custom View ID) or one of the search parameters (`criteria`, `phone`, `email`, `word`).

**Important Constraint (Zoho Documentation):**

You can only include **either** `cvid` **or** one of the search parameters (`criteria`, `phone`, `email`, `word`) in a single request. Combining `cvid` with any search parameter will result in an `AMBIGUITY_DURING_PROCESSING` error (HTTP 400).

delete.description: To permanently delete one or more records from the Recycle Bin in your Zoho CRM account. When deleting a parent record, Zoho CRM also removes all its associated child records from the Recycle Bin, such as Notes and Attachments. When the total number of records to delete is 1000 or fewer, the operation completes immediately and returns a 200 response with per-item results. When the total exceeds 1000, the deletion runs as a background job and returns a 202 response. Partial successes return a 207 multi-status response with individual success and error entries per record.

post.description: To restore one or more deleted records from the Recycle Bin in your Zoho CRM account. Supply the scope of restoration in the request body using exactly one of three options: **ids** to restore specific records, **filters** to restore records matching field-based criteria, or **restore_all_records** to restore every record currently in the Recycle Bin. When restoring a parent record, Zoho CRM also restores all its associated child records, such as Notes and Attachments. If the total number of records to restore, including child records, is 1000 or fewer, the operation completes immediately. When the total exceeds 1000, when the **filters** option is applied, or when **restore_all_records** is **true**, the restoration runs as a background job. Admin users can restore any record; non-admin users can restore only the records they own unless their profile grants broader access.

comparator.description: Specify the comparison operator to apply between the field and the value. Possible values: **equal**, **not_equal**, **contains**, **not_contains**, **starts_with**, **ends_with**, **greater_than**, **less_than**. The set of comparators supported depends on the field: **display_name** and **deleted_by** support equal, not_equal, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with; **module** supports equal and not_equal; **deleted_time** supports equal, not_equal, greater_than, less_than.

Each rule includes its field-based criteria, touch-point signal rules, custom score fields, layout, module, and audit metadata. Returns 204 with no body if no scoring rules are configured.

put.description: Updates one or more scoring rules. Returns 200 (all success) or 207 (partial success).
put.x-zs-llm-description:
Bulk-updates one or more scoring rules in a single request. Each rule in `scoring_rules` must identify the target via `id`. Partial updates are supported - only include fields that need to change; omitted fields are left unchanged.

**Updatable fields per rule:**
- `name` - rename the scoring rule.
- `description` - update the rule description.
- `active` - enable or disable the rule.
- `field_rules` - CRM field criteria mapped to scores. Each entry needs `criteria` and `score`.
- `signal_rules` - interaction signal rules. To delete an entry, supply its `id` with `_delete: null`.
- `custom_fields` - reassign or rename score field mappings (up to 6). To delete an entry, supply its `id` with `_delete: null`.

**Deleting nested entries with `_delete`:**
To remove an individual `signal_rule` or `custom_field` entry without replacing the entire array, include its `id` and set `_delete: null`.

Returns 200 if all succeed, 207 (multi-status) if some fail.

post.description: Creates one or more scoring rules for specified modules and layouts. Only Leads and Contacts modules support signal rules. Deals, Accounts and Custom Modules do not support signal rules.
post.x-zs-llm-description:
Creates one or more scoring rules. Up to 10 rules per layout. Each rule requires `module` and `name`.

**Required fields:**
- `name` - scoring rule name.
- `module` - CRM module (e.g., Leads, Contacts).
- For Leads and Contacts: at least one of `field_rules` or `signal_rules` is required.
- For other modules: `field_rules` is required.

**field_rules** - CRM field criteria mapped to scores. Each entry needs `criteria` (filter on a CRM field) and `score` (integer, -100 to 100).

**signal_rules** - interaction signal criteria. Each entry needs `signal` (with `namespace` and `id`) and `score`.

**Optional:** `description`, `active` (default true), `layout` (null means all layouts), `custom_fields` (up to 6 CRM score field mappings).

Returns 201 if all rules are created. Returns 207 (multi-status) if some fail.

put.x-zs-llm-description:
Updates an existing scoring rule identified by the `ruleId` path parameter. The request body must contain a `scoring_rules` array with exactly one rule object. Partial updates are supported - only include the top-level fields that need to change.

**Updatable fields:**
- `name` - rename the scoring rule.
- `description` - update the rule description.
- `active` - enable or disable the rule.
- `field_rules` - CRM field criteria mapped to scores. Each entry needs `criteria` and `score`.
- `signal_rules` - interaction signal rules. Each entry needs `signal` and `score`. To delete a `signal_rule` entry, include its `id` with `_delete: null`.
- `custom_fields` - reassign or rename CRM score field mappings (up to 6). To delete a mapping, supply its `id` with `_delete: null`.

**Deleting nested entries with `_delete`:**
To remove an individual `field_rule` or `signal_rule` or `custom_field` entry without replacing the entire array, include the entry's `id` and set `_delete: null`.

Returns 200 on success.
